name: Package root with front doors
description: Imports the layers, installs the cross-layer wiring that keeps core independent of adapters and runner, and exposes version, config loading and a client front door that share one config file with a lane.
advantages: One import gives a consumer a documented, stable entry point and keeps layering clean.
disadvantages: Import-time wiring is global state, so order matters, and the exported name list must be maintained by hand.

name: Long-lived background loop bridge
description: Runs coroutines and blocking work from synchronous adapter code on one lazily created daemon event loop, with a blocking call and a fire-and-forget call on a bounded executor.
advantages: Fixes the failure where an async client binds to the first loop and breaks later, so no consumer needs its own copy.
disadvantages: A single shared loop is a global resource and a long blocking task can delay others; it is invisible until misused.

name: Live package-surface driver
description: Imports the real package, checks names and registrations, calls the front doors in a scrubbed environment, runs the bridge, signature probes, strippers, report builders and edit parser, and imports modules in a subprocess whose sockets refuse.
advantages: Tests the promised surface exactly as a consumer meets it, with no model or network. Selected because: quest_ai_runner/__init__.py (the package root, load_config, load_client), take_in_the_world/async_bridge.py, core/scaffolding.py, bootstrap_email.py, vendor/
disadvantages: The name list is hand-written, so a new name is covered only once a case is added.

name: Minimal lane example
description: A short script that builds a config from a file and the environment and hands it to the shared lane driver, showing check, once and loop-forever modes.
advantages: Shows the smallest working lane and the contrast with hand-rolled drivers.
disadvantages: Hides detail by design, so customisation needs the second example and the docs.

name: Custom consumer configuration example
description: Builds a full runner configuration for an organisation entirely from environment variables with safe placeholders, covering model backend choice, corpus, deep-runner path and optional context settings.
advantages: A copyable reference for the many options of a real deployment, usable unchanged across environments.
disadvantages: Long and option-heavy, so a newcomer may be overwhelmed and the comments can go stale.

name: Example check harness
description: Compiles and imports each example, runs it as a subprocess in a scrubbed environment, calls the demo stub provider, loads the sample config, and checks index coverage and a secret and path scan. Backed at run time by the arms minimal_lane and custom_consumer (the reference consumers in examples/); this arm runs them and stays selected as the measured one.
advantages: Catches a broken or leaking example before a newcomer does, with no model or network. Selected because: examples/ as shipped (README.md lists each file)
disadvantages: Does not run demos that need a live backend or terminal to completion.

name: Configuration dataclass and file entry point
description: The runner configuration dataclass declares every field, which of them a file may express, and the from-file constructor that hands the file to the loader. It is the single place where the set of settable fields lives, so adding a field and making it file-expressible happen together.
advantages: One typed object holds every setting, so consumers have a single contract and the file-expressible set cannot drift from the fields.
disadvantages: The module is large and mixes field declarations with resolution helpers, so it is slow to read and easy to over-extend.

name: Strict TOML file loader
description: Parses the TOML file into the configuration, using the field set passed in by the dataclass, and raises a configuration-file error on anything a file cannot express: unknown keys, adapter-only objects and malformed values. The personas table is read here as a structured section.
advantages: Fails loudly and early with the offending key named, which removes silent typos.
disadvantages: Strictness means any new field must be registered as file-expressible before it can be used, and it cannot express live objects such as adapters.

name: Environment and env-file layering
description: Applies environment files and the file's own environment tables to the process with defined precedence: a process variable beats env files, which beat the file's environment table, and an earlier env file wins over a later one. It also treats blank placeholder values as unset so defaults still apply.
advantages: Lets one file serve as a baseline while an operator overrides a single value without editing it; precedence is deterministic.
disadvantages: Mutating the process environment is a global side effect, so ordering bugs show up as action at a distance and tests must scrub the environment.

name: Environment-backed tuning settings
description: Parses the tunables the core package needs (timeouts, caps, floors, review interval) from the environment into one typed settings value, falling back to the shipped default on a bad value and allowing zero to switch a feature off. The provider re-reads the environment on each call unless a fixed value is pinned.
advantages: A malformed value can never stop a lane, and a running process can be retuned without a restart.
disadvantages: Silent fallback hides a typo in a tuning value, unlike the loud rejection used for file keys; re-reading on every call costs a little work per use.

name: Injected core settings holder
description: Defines the typed settings value and the install and read functions, so the core package asks for its tunables at the point of use instead of touching the process environment. A consumer can pin a fixed value or supply a provider.
advantages: Keeps the core package free of environment reads and makes it testable with fixed settings.
disadvantages: Core code relies on a globally installed provider, so a missing install gives surprising defaults.

name: Layered configuration evaluation arm
description: Drives the live loaders offline: the file alone through the from-file constructor, the layered startup path through the same function the command line uses, and the tuning settings, scrubbing the process environment and faking nothing else. It is the measured arm for the real configuration path, scored on rule-by-rule cases. Backed at run time by the arms config, config_file, config_environment, config_core_settings and runtime_settings; this arm measures them and stays selected as the measured one, so the runtime arm is not promoted over it.
advantages: Exercises the real code, so a precedence regression fails a case directly, with zero model calls. Selected because: cli_config._config_from_env (QAR_CONFIG_FILE or --config)
disadvantages: Covers the commonly set scalar fields, not every field, so a rarely used field can regress unnoticed.

name: Command dispatcher
description: The entry point builds the parser, routes each subcommand to its handler and converts outcomes into exit codes. Store commands and Quest commands are delegated to their own modules so the dispatcher stays a thin router.
advantages: One entry point gives a consistent exit-code contract across all subcommands.
disadvantages: It also hosts interactive surfaces that are not scored, so a regression there is not caught by the offline cases.

name: Declarative argument tree
description: Defines the whole argparse tree for every subcommand in one place, with help text and flag definitions, so parsing and usage errors come from the parser itself.
advantages: Help and refusal behaviour for unknown commands and flags is uniform and cheap to test.
disadvantages: Behaviour that depends on cross-flag rules lives in handlers, not here, so the parser alone does not guarantee valid combinations.

name: Quest API subcommands
description: Implements the generic quest command, send, reconcile-plan, create-goal and folder sync by introspecting the Quest client's methods, refusing write methods unless a write flag is given, and parsing keyword pairs as JSON when possible.
advantages: A new client method becomes callable from the shell without new CLI code, with a safe read-only default.
disadvantages: Introspection means the help text is only as good as the client docstrings, and a pair value that happens to parse as JSON is not passed as a string.

name: Card-store maintenance commands
description: Provides the context subcommands for moving a store root, migrating imports, merging stores, showing info and uploading a local store, all as a dry run unless an apply flag is given, and none of them embeds anything.
advantages: Dry-run by default protects stores from accidental change and shows what would happen.
disadvantages: Operations on real stores and vector points are hard to simulate fully, so most of the risk is covered only on a scratch folder.

name: Tool catalog shell entry
description: Lets a deep run's shell list, show and call the same tools the brain uses in process, rebuilding the catalog from the lane's environment and accepting arguments as keyword pairs or one JSON object, with keyword pairs winning.
advantages: A shell can use the same tools as the brain with no second implementation, and custom tools appear automatically.
disadvantages: Argument typing by JSON guessing can surprise a caller, and a call acts for real when the tool does.

name: Real-entry-point evaluation arm
description: Calls the live main functions in process with a scrubbed environment and a scratch folder, capturing output and exit code, and fakes nothing. It is the measured arm for the command-line surface.
advantages: Tests the actual entry points end to end without a subprocess, so it is fast and offline. Selected because: pyproject console script quest-ai-runner and python -m quest_ai_runner tools
disadvantages: In-process calls do not cover the console-script wrapper or terminal behaviour, and interactive modes are out of reach.

name: Documentation index
description: The index document that groups tutorials, guides and references and links every other document, so a reader or an AI starts in one place and every document is reachable.
advantages: A single entry point makes orphan detection simple and onboarding quick.
disadvantages: Needs manual upkeep, and a linked document may still be unclear or outdated.

name: Shipped-documents evaluation arm
description: Resolves relative links on disk, counts em dashes, reads the index and the generated configuration reference, and consults the live package for its public names and real subcommands to confirm each is documented. Backed at run time by the arm README.md (the shipped docs folder, docs/README.md); this arm measures it and stays selected as the measured one.
advantages: Checks the docs as shipped against the live code, with zero model calls. Selected because: docs/README.md (the index), docs/reference/configuration.md (generated), README.md
disadvantages: Checks presence and form, not whether a description is accurate or helpful.

name: Rules only, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. Classification is by command shape and the acknowledgement is a fixed line.
advantages: No cost, instant.
disadvantages: Fails on free-form asks; not built.

name: Apply the evolvable-structure library
description: QAR keeps its specifications as records under esoi and builds on the library's solutions to apply a project's structure: the application procedure, the structure check, the measurement harness and the implementation selector.
advantages: No checker of QAR's own to maintain; every part is compared on the same cases and selected by its metric. Selected because: the evolvable-structure library already carries the machinery; QAR keeps only its records and configuration
disadvantages: A dependency pinned by commit, and a runtime one because implementations are declared with its decorators; a rule or format change in the library needs a migration here; offline arms only unless a paid arm is run by decision.

name: Offline suite configuration
description: Keeps the test suite offline by configuring collection and fixtures.
advantages: No test reaches a network or a model by accident.
disadvantages: A missing fixture only fails at setup, and collection says nothing about whether a test passes.

name: Collection check by test file
description: . Backed at run time by the arm conftest (tests/conftest.py, which keeps the suite offline); this arm measures it and stays selected as the measured one.
advantages: Selected because: CLAUDE.md pre-commit rule: run only the tests your change touches; this collection check is the cheap whole-suite gate
disadvantages: Collection proves tests import and parametrise, not that they pass or stay offline.

name: Planted-secret evaluation arm
description: Runs the live scanner on text assembled from fragments (so the test file itself is clean), on groups of real repository files, and as a command in a throwaway git repository. No runtime arm in this repository backs it: the scanner is the hub's secret redaction, to which adapters/files_redaction.py adds only the Quest key shape; the evaluation arm stays selected.
advantages: Proves both detection and silence on placeholders against the real scanner, without keeping real secrets anywhere. Selected because: `esoi hygiene` (CLAUDE.md pre-commit step 2, docs/how-to/public-hygiene.md)
disadvantages: Planted cases only cover the shapes someone thought to add.

name: Problem-linked tag list with a check rule and a lookup
description: esoi/tags.csv holds each tag with a one-sentence meaning and the problems it mitigates (problem_ids); solutions carry tags in their tags column; the QAR rule Q1 in scripts/esoi_tags.py (registered by the plugin scripts/esoi_rules.py) fails a tag outside the list, a listed tag with no meaning, with no linked problem or with a linked id that is not a problem record, and a tag used by no solution or by every solution, and prints a note for a tag on one solution. tags_of and solutions_sharing (and the script run as a command) read a solution's tags as its column plus its problem_ids.
advantages: One list as the source of truth; every tag's risk is a problem record that can be read, linked and solved; the lookup uses the links that already exist, so problem ids are never copied.
disadvantages: The rule cannot judge whether a tag mitigates its risk or whether a link already identifies the same solutions; that rests on the back-fill procedure and, later, on the metric. R1 to R4 are recorded in this project, not yet in the library that owns them.
